US.hint: 50 white stars on blue with 13 red and white stripes.
US.funFact: The 50-star design came from a 17-year-old's school project, which got a B-minus.

CA.hint: Red, white, red vertical with a red 11-pointed maple leaf.
CA.funFact: Canada has the longest coastline of any country.

MX.hint: Green, white, red vertical with an eagle eating a snake on a cactus.
MX.funFact: The eagle comes from the Aztec legend of founding Tenochtitlan, now Mexico City.

BZ.hint: Blue with red stripes top and bottom and a detailed coat of arms showing two woodcutters.
BZ.funFact: It's one of the very few national flags that shows people.

CR.hint: Blue, white, a thick red, white, blue stripes, with a coat of arms on the red.
CR.funFact: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948.

SV.hint: Blue, white, blue with a triangle coat of arms circled by gold writing.
SV.funFact: In 2021 El Salvador became the first country to make Bitcoin legal tender.

GT.hint: Sky blue, white, sky blue vertical with a green quetzal bird and crossed rifles.
GT.funFact: Guatemala's currency, the quetzal, is named after its national bird.

HN.hint: Blue, white, blue horizontal with five blue stars in an X pattern.
HN.funFact: The five stars stand for the five nations of the old Federal Republic of Central America.

NI.hint: Blue, white, blue with a triangle emblem showing volcanoes and a rainbow.
NI.funFact: Nicaragua's rainbow makes it one of only two national flags with purple (the other is Dominica).

PA.hint: Four squares: white with a blue star, red, blue, and white with a red star.
PA.funFact: The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

AG.hint: Red with a black, blue and white V-shape and a golden rising sun.
AG.funFact: Antigua is said to have 365 beaches, one for every day of the year.

BS.hint: Aquamarine, gold, aquamarine stripes with a black triangle at the flagpole.
BS.funFact: Christopher Columbus first landed in the Americas in the Bahamas in 1492.

BB.hint: Blue, gold, blue vertical with a black trident head in the middle.
BB.funFact: Barbados became a republic in 2021, replacing the British monarch as head of state.

CU.hint: Five blue and white stripes with a red triangle and a white star.
CU.funFact: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

DM.hint: Green with a yellow-black-white cross and a red circle holding a purple Sisserou parrot.
DM.funFact: Dominica is one of only two national flags with purple, thanks to its parrot.

DO.hint: A white cross dividing blue and red squares, with a coat of arms that includes a Bible.
DO.funFact: It's the only national flag that shows an open Bible.

GD.hint: Red border with six yellow stars, yellow and green triangles, and a nutmeg on the left.
GD.funFact: Grenada is the 'Island of Spice', and the nutmeg on its flag celebrates its famous crop.

HT.hint: Blue over red with a white panel holding a coat of arms with a palm tree and cannons.
HT.funFact: Haiti was the first nation founded by formerly enslaved people, independent in 1804.

JM.hint: A gold diagonal cross with green and black triangles, and no red, white or blue.
JM.funFact: Jamaica's is the only national flag without any red, white or blue.

KN.hint: A black diagonal band edged in yellow with two white stars, between green and red.
KN.funFact: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Western Hemisphere.

LC.hint: Light blue with black, white and gold triangles: the twin Piton mountains.
LC.funFact: Saint Lucia is said to be the only country named after a woman (Saint Lucy).

VC.hint: Blue, gold, green vertical with three green diamonds in a V shape.
VC.funFact: The diamonds form a 'V' for Vincent; the islands are nicknamed 'the Gems of the Antilles'.

TT.hint: Red with a black diagonal stripe edged in white.
TT.funFact: The steelpan drum was invented in Trinidad and Tobago in the 20th century.

AR.hint: Light blue, white, light blue with a golden 'Sun of May' that has a face.
AR.funFact: Argentina's name comes from argentum, Latin for silver.

BO.hint: Red, yellow, green horizontal with a coat of arms. Ghana has the same colours but a black star.
BO.funFact: Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in the world.

BR.hint: Green with a yellow diamond and a blue starry globe with the words 'Ordem e Progresso'.
BR.funFact: The stars show the sky over Rio de Janeiro on 15 November 1889, the day Brazil became a republic.

CL.hint: White over red with a blue square and a white star, a bit like the Texas flag.
CL.funFact: Chile's Atacama is the driest non-polar desert in the world.

CO.hint: Yellow, blue, red horizontal, with yellow taking up the whole top half.
CO.funFact: Colombia is the world's leading producer of emeralds.

EC.hint: Yellow, blue, red like Colombia, but with a coat of arms with a condor.
EC.funFact: Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through it.

GY.hint: Green with a white-edged golden arrowhead and a black-edged red triangle: 'The Golden Arrowhead'.
GY.funFact: Guyana is the only South American country where English is the official language.

PY.hint: Red, white, blue horizontal with an emblem. The front and back of the flag are different!
PY.funFact: Paraguay shares the Itaipu Dam with Brazil, one of the biggest hydroelectric dams on Earth.

PE.hint: Red, white, red vertical: Canada's colours without the maple leaf.
PE.funFact: Machu Picchu, the Inca citadel in the Andes, is in Peru.

SR.hint: Green, white, a wide red, white, green stripes with a yellow star in the middle.
SR.funFact: Suriname is the most forested country in the world, with more than 90% forest cover.

UY.hint: Nine white and blue stripes with a golden 'Sun of May' in the top-left white square.
UY.funFact: Uruguay hosted and won the very first FIFA World Cup, in 1930.

VE.hint: Yellow, blue, red with an arc of eight white stars on the blue.
VE.funFact: Venezuela's Angel Falls is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall in the world.
